source.title: Good volatility, bad volatility, and the cross section of cryptocurrency returns

hypothesis: Cryptocurrencies with lower lagged relative signed jump variation earn higher subsequent weekly returns.
universe: Binance USD-M USDT perpetuals already listed by 2021-12-31, including later-delisted contracts when data exist; each Monday retain top 50 by lagged trailing-30-day quote volume.
feature: For each complete UTC day, compute positive and negative hourly log-return semivariances; daily RSJ=(RV_plus-RV_minus)/(RV_plus+RV_minus). At Monday open use the lagged rolling mean RSJ over W completed days.
signal_direction: Negative: long lowest RSJ quintile, short highest RSJ quintile.
portfolio: Equal-weight long bottom-RSJ quintile and short top-RSJ quintile, 0.5 gross each side.
rebalance: Weekly Monday 00:00 UTC using data through Sunday 23:00 UTC; execute at Monday open.
development_gate: Canonical mean rank IC of -RSJ >0.02, positive bottom-minus-top RSJ return spread, canonical net Sharpe >0.70, and at least 2/3 lookbacks positive.
success_gate: Canonical OOS net Sharpe >1.0, positive at 2x costs, >=2/3 lookbacks positive, 2024 and 2025 non-negative, max drawdown <35%, excluding BTC/ETH and strongest contributor positive.
notes: The paper uses high-frequency data and documents a negative RSJ-return relation. Hourly Binance data is a coarser but still intraday non-parametric implementation; this deviation is fixed before results.
